question: Do local in-context examples from the full fitting set let TabDPT 1.1 contribute more than the two prior random 512-row contexts? Its global one-hot proposal improved one confirmation panel but regressed on the other.
setup: Use just the prior nomination-selected one-hot representation and the same verified 307497212-byte checkpoint. Fit the official frozen model's feature preprocessing and index once on all 4,061 fitting rows. For each of the 2,432 development queries run the publisher's nearest-neighbour context inference at 128 and 512 rows. This tests the change in both support availability and retrieval; it does not isolate a single causal factor. No new task-specific features, no external data, no query labels. Bound GPU memory using inference batches of 8. Persist the first output in case the second context size exceeds machine resources.
decision: Compare the two actual retrieval sizes with retention through the same 808/817/807 nomination/confirmation rule. Require no confirmation panel to regress and pooled gain of .003 vs the research pair to justify a larger blinded test. Count one full frozen context fit, one fitted feature encoder, and distinguish the 4,864 query contexts from classifier training or paid API calls.
